clinical_category: Status epilepticus - seizure-type-specific operational time points
blueprint_topic: Recognition of prolonged seizure physiology using current status-epilepticus definitions
stem: A nurse reviews the ILAE operational concept of status epilepticus. Which statement is accurate?

options.A: The operational time point for treatment depends on seizure type; for tonic-clonic status epilepticus, t1 is 5 minutes rather than a universal 5-minute definition for every seizure type
options.B: Every form of status epilepticus uses exactly the same 5-minute t1 and 30-minute t2 thresholds
options.C: Treatment of tonic-clonic status epilepticus should generally be delayed until the seizure has continued for 30 minutes
options.D: The ILAE no longer uses time-based operational concepts when describing status epilepticus

rationale: A is correct. The ILAE status-epilepticus framework uses operational time points that vary with seizure type. For tonic-clonic status epilepticus, t1 is 5 minutes—the point at which ongoing seizure activity is unlikely to stop spontaneously and treatment should begin—while t2 is approximately 30 minutes, reflecting increasing concern for long-term consequences such as neuronal injury. Other status-epilepticus types have different operational time points. B incorrectly turns seizure-type-specific values into universal thresholds. C confuses the later t2 concept with the time to start treatment. D contradicts the current ILAE status-epilepticus framework. This item is distinct from V2-Q1967 and V2-Q1968 because it tests the definition's seizure-type-specific t1/t2 concept rather than emergency escalation or first-line treatment.
educational_objective: Understand that status-epilepticus operational time points are seizure-type specific; for tonic-clonic status epilepticus, treatment begins at the 5-minute t1 point rather than waiting for the later t2 period associated with increasing risk of long-term injury.
source_document_title: A definition and classification of status epilepticus — Report of the ILAE Task Force on Classification of Status Epilepticus; What's new in status epilepticus
source_version_date: ILAE Task Force definition published 2015 and still listed by ILAE among its definition/classification documents; 2025 ILAE update interview reiterates t1=5 minutes and t2≈30 minutes for tonic-clonic status epilepticus; currentness checked 2026-08-18
source_locator: ILAE Definition & Classification → 'A definition and classification of status epilepticus' remains listed under other definition/classification documents. ILAE 2025 'What's new in status epilepticus' → tonic-clonic seizure activity lasting more than 5 minutes corresponds to t1, when spontaneous termination is unlikely and treatment should start; t2 is around 30 minutes and relates to neuronal injury/network alteration; the discussion explicitly notes that these values apply to tonic-clonic status and that other status types differ.
source_claim_supported: Current ILAE resources directly support seizure-type-specific operational status-epilepticus time points and specifically support t1=5 minutes and t2≈30 minutes for tonic-clonic status epilepticus.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Physiological Adaptation client-needs subcategory (11–17% of items); this item tests recognition of a prolonged neurologic emergency and the physiologic significance of time-sensitive seizure progression.
correction_summary: Total construct rebuild for precision and duplicate avoidance. The original generic AAN item implied a broadly uniform 5-minute definition. The final item uses current ILAE resources to teach that operational time points depend on seizure type and distinguishes tonic-clonic t1 from t2 without duplicating the emergency-response construct already tested in V2-Q1967 or the benzodiazepine-treatment construct in V2-Q1968.
audit_findings: The source item's wording overgeneralized the 5-minute concept across status-epilepticus types.
ILAE continues to list the 2015 status-epilepticus definition/classification and a 2025 ILAE update explicitly reiterates the tonic-clonic t1/t2 framework.
The final answer explicitly limits the 5-minute t1 to tonic-clonic status epilepticus and does not treat it as a universal threshold for every form.
The construct is distinct from V2-Q1967 and V2-Q1968 by testing definition/time-point interpretation rather than escalation or drug treatment.
Independent adversarial second pass found one uniquely correct answer, no second defensible option, no unsupported universal timing rule, no cueing, and no unresolved conflict.
